messages:
Anya: quick thought — is route-level debounce + quota gating something we want in the console or keep it infra-only? :thinking:
Sam: i'm leaning infra-only. console UX for this gets messy fast. UX surface: when a saved query triggers a debounce, users might think it's a bug.
Bryan: agree on UX risk. but we do need a clear affordance for "cost previews" and when sampling/quota kicks in. otherwise product teams will be surprised by token burn.
Marta: what if we show a small badge on saved queries: 'sampled (50%)' + hover explains quota gating and provides a 'run full' button gated by permission? keeps console visible but not noisy.
Anya: that could work. i want to avoid modal spamming. badge + lightweight toast seems ok. how do we map debounce to routing policy though? example: route X should debounce at 300ms for quick nav but not for scheduled sampling.
Sam: suggest policy separation: "interactive" vs "batch" modes. console quick preview = interactive => debounce 250-500ms, sampling/export = batch => no debounce, honor max_tokens/quota thresholds.
Bryan: API side we'd need request metadata: {"mode":"interactive"} or header x-redwood-mode. frontend can set that. will that break existing savedquery replay?
Marta: frontend change only, fallback default to interactive if not provided. for saved query run from API (e.g. scheduled) we set batch. need migration path in docs and telemetry to detect bad clients.
Anya: okay, also telemetry: we should record when debounce suppressed a call and when quota gating returned a sampled response. fields: route_id, mode, debounce_ms, sampled_pct, quota_action (none/partial/blocked).
Sam: +1. add a boolean 'user_forced_full' when someone clicks "run full" from console so we can measure how often people bypass sampling.
Bryan: implementor note: runtime can do prefix cache + sampling; quota gating should be done at router to avoid charging downstream. router decisions logged with request_id.
Marta: UX text for badge draft: "Sampled — results show a subset to reduce cost. Click to run full (may use quota)." keep it short.
Anya: will create a tiny RFC doc with UI mock, API header pattern, and telemetry schema. pinging @deploy-bot to add an RFC checklist item.
deploy-bot: created issue #4122: "console: route debounce + quota-gating RFC" — assignees: Anya, Sam, Bryan, Marta. link: https://redwood-inference.internal/issue/4122
Sam: timeline? aiming for a small canary in next sprint (2 weeks) to collect telemetry.
Marta: i'll mock the badge and hover copy today and drop in Figma.
Anya: thanks all. we'll iterate on wording after some telemetry comes in. :thumbsup:
thread_text_preview: Anya kicks off a short thread about adding debounce + quota gating visibility in console. Team agrees on separation of interactive vs batch modes, an API header, telemetry fields, and a small UI badge with a 'run full' affordance. deploy-bot files RFC.
